goal: Makes sure a failed block or undo file flush always triggers the flush-error notification, even if a future code path forgets to call it.
Builds on PR #35714 which stops the node from continuing to write chainstate data after a flush failure.
reviewability: Author explicitly asks not to review until base PR #35714 lands, and CI is currently failing.

result.summary: This PR hardens the invariant that any failed block or undo file flush emits the flush-error notification, so FlushStateToDisk's early-return-on-error logic (added in #35714) can rely on AbortNode always being triggered. It introduces a FlushFile() helper that couples the flush call and the notification, and adds BlockManager-level unit tests that inject block-file and undo-file failures separately to assert the notification fires each time. It contains the two commits from #35714 plus two new commits (test coverage and the FlushFile refactor), and is explicitly marked not to be reviewed before #35714.
result.problem: Currently, FlushStateToDisk() assumes that every branch which sets success=false inside FlushBlockFile/FlushUndoFile has already emitted the flush-error notification, but that assumption is not enforced by the code structure. A future flush-failure branch that forgets to notify would cause the node to return an error without calling AbortNode, silently continuing without a proper shutdown, an integrity risk for chainstate maintainers.

categories.evidence: Includes the #35714 commit 'validation: stop writes after flush failure' which changes Chainstate::FlushStateToDisk to return an error and stop writing block-index/coins data instead of only logging a warning, directly altering chainstate flush behavior.
categories.rationale: Commit message states: 'When a block-file or undo-file flush fails, shutdown is requested, but FlushStateToDisk() still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances m_last_flushed_block' -- a chainstate integrity bug where failed flushes could leave inconsistent last-flushed-block bookkeeping. Fixing this and hardening the notification invariant protects chainstate correctness on I/O failure, though it depends on and duplicates commits already under review in #35714.

result.card: This draft PR hardens the flush-error notification invariant in block storage so that any failed block or undo file flush is guaranteed to emit a flushError notification, preventing a future code path from silently skipping AbortNode. It is explicitly a follow-up to #35714 ('validation: stop writes after flush failure'), containing that PR's two commits plus a FlushFile() encapsulation and new BlockManager-level unit tests that inject block-file and undo-file failures separately. The author states directly: 'do not merge or review before that PR', and CI is currently failing, so review should start at #35714. No reviewers have yet commented on either PR. The underlying problem, silent continuation after a failed flush, is a real chainstate-integrity risk described in the commit message as writing metadata and advancing m_last_flushed_block even after a flush failure, but it is a hardening/preventive fix rather than an active reported bug.
